title: orchestrate plugin config
description: Tuning knobs for the orchestrate router. The active harness resolves its profile first; explicit role values then override it. Config is layered (deep-merged, first present wins per key).

autonomy.description: How autonomous the orchestrator is once it has classified the task and built a plan. propose = announce the workflow + plan and wait for OK (default); auto = run immediately; threshold = auto only when under the threshold limits, otherwise propose.

harness.description: auto selects from the running agent runtime's delegation capability; claude and codex force one profile. Use a forced profile only for a known harness-specific installation.

threshold.description: Limits used when autonomy=threshold. At or below these, fan out automatically; above either, propose first.

roles.description: Explicit model overrides for the roles. auto takes the role from the active harness profile. Use only model IDs or aliases supported by the running harness.

senior.description: Builder for work-graph nodes classified as hard. auto resolves to harnessProfiles.<harness>.roles.senior, else that profile's top tier (its orchestrator model) — so it is always a stronger model than the builder without naming one.

manager.description: Large-build manager: owns the plan, merge order and decision ledger. auto = the resolved orchestrator role (this session). Another advertised model spawns one manager agent at that model.

lead.description: Large-build workstream lead: runs one workstream's builders and verifiers. auto = the resolved senior role (the profile's top tier unless senior is set).

harnessProfiles.description: Per-harness fallback models. These are defaults, not a capability registry: when a runtime exposes a different supported-model list, update this profile or leave roles as auto to inherit the runtime default.

workflows.description: Which pre-curated workflows the router may select, and per-workflow fan-out caps. A disabled workflow is never routed to; the router falls back to the closest enabled workflow or asks.

worktrees.description: Git worktree isolation for writing nodes of the work graph. Worktrees are created, merged, and removed only through the skill's bundled scripts/worktree.sh.

mode.description: auto = a worktree per writing node whenever two or more run concurrently; always = a worktree for every writing node; off = builders share the main checkout.

cleanup.description: on-success = remove merged worktrees and keep any with unmerged or uncommitted work for inspection; always = force-remove every worktree of the run at the end, discarding unmerged work.

link.description: Gitignored paths (relative to the repo root) symlinked from the main checkout into each new worktree so nodes can build and test, e.g. ["node_modules", ".venv", ".env"]. Shared, not copied: nodes must not install packages through them.

setup.description: Optional command run inside each new worktree before its builder starts (e.g. "npm ci"). Runs as an ordinary command under normal permissions, never through the pre-approved worktree script.

escalation.description: Cascade behavior: re-run a single failed or thin leg one tier up before giving up.

builderToSenior.description: When a builder-tier node fails verification or reports the contract is insufficient, re-run that one node once at the senior tier in a fresh worktree. Does not count against maxSenior.

largeBuild.description: Large-build mode: an implement run managed in workstreams, with a manager, two or three leads, a decision ledger and checkpoints. See skills/orchestrate/workflows/large-build.md.

enabled.description: Whether the router may switch an implement run to large-build on its own. An explicit "large build" request is honored either way.

minWorkstreams.description: Auto-switch only when the work graph, minus its contract node(s), splits into at least this many independent workstreams.

minNodes.description: Auto-switch only when the work graph also has at least this many writing nodes.

maxLeads.description: Cap on workstream leads. Workstreams beyond it are grouped so each lead owns one area.

maxParallel.description: Cap on concurrent builders and verifiers across all leads. Each lead is also capped at workflows.implement.maxParallel.

ledger.description: Decision ledger path, relative to the main checkout; <run> is replaced by the run id. The only place design calls are written; only the manager writes it.

projectLog.description: Where durable decisions (behavior, spec/contract, money, cost, vendor, data shape) are also written. auto = detect the project's decision log (named in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, decision-log.md, DECISIONS.md, an ADR directory); a path = that file or ADR directory, relative to the main checkout; none = no project log, copy them into the MR/PR description and the final report.

status.description: Status file path, relative to the main checkout; <run> is replaced by the run id. Rewritten at every checkpoint so a resumed or replacement manager can continue.

doctrine.description: How forcefully the SessionStart hook injects the delegation doctrine. off = no injection; standard = inject as guidance; strict = inject as a hard rule.

alwaysPassModelExplicitly.description: Instruct the orchestrator to pass the model parameter explicitly on every Agent call, working around the frontmatter model bug (anthropics/claude-code#44385).

maxParallel.description: Cap on parallel fan-out agents for this workflow. Guards against the over-fan-out failure mode (Anthropic multi-agent research: fan-out is ~15x the tokens of a single pass).

maxSenior.description: Cap on work-graph nodes classified to the senior tier per run (escalations excluded). Needing more usually means the prelude contract is unfinished.
